probes.why: Advertises the routing prefix and vendor overrides. Everything else depends on what this returns.
The baseline read. If this 404s the prefix is wrong, not the catalog.
Pagination is optional in the spec. Who honours pageSize, who ignores it?
Multi-level namespaces. OneLake documents that it does NOT support the parent param, so this cell is a known negative going in.
Namespace properties round-trip.
Existence check without a body. Commonly unimplemented.
Table listing within a namespace.
The load-bearing call. Feeds the entire field tier below.
Full snapshot history vs. the refs-only default. Time travel depends on it.
Existence check without a body.
Vended storage credentials. The newest and least evenly adopted endpoint.
Iceberg views are a separate spec section and adoption is patchy.
Server-side scan planning. Recent addition; expect mostly 404/501.
Metrics reporting. Widely stubbed to 204 without storing anything. Body must be a complete ScanReport or a 400 tells you nothing.
First real write. OneLake is documented read-only, so this is where that shows up as a status code.
Property updates are separately optional from namespace creation.
Table creation with an explicit schema, partition spec and sort order — checks whether all three survive a round-trip.
A property-set commit — the cheapest possible exercise of the update path.
remove-properties: the inverse of the one action every catalog serves.

add-schema together with set-current-schema:-1 in a single commit. That pairing is the spec's idiom -- -1 means the schema added by this same request, so splitting them across two commits is meaningless.
set-current-schema naming an existing schema (0), exercising the action on its own rather than as part of an add-schema commit.
upgrade-format-version to 2. The fixture is already v2, so this is a no-op for a conformant server -- rejecting it is the finding.
Multi-table atomic commit. Rarely implemented; a clean differentiator. Carries one real change: an empty transaction gets rejected as invalid, which would be indistinguishable from unimplemented.
Rename is one of the most commonly missing write endpoints.
Whether purgeRequested is honoured. Purge semantics vary widely and several catalogs gate it behind a server flag.
Plain drop, and the cleanup that must succeed. A 404 here is the expected outcome when the purge drop above already removed the table.
createView with a minimal SQL representation.
loadView -- the read counterpart of loadTable for views.
viewExists.
replaceView: a property-set commit against the view.
renameView -- separate from renameTable in the spec.
dropView, and the cleanup that must succeed before the namespace goes.
Cleanup.
